subject: SIG follow-up: Data discipline, ephemeral telemetry, and model-training guarantees
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@medicahealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@medicahealth.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: questions on logs, retention, training

Connor — thanks again for walking our security team through the SIG baseline on Wednesday. A couple of follow-ups from our side so we can close out the control gaps:  

1) Prompt/interaction logs: Do you persist raw prompts or chat transcripts beyond what is absolutely necessary for serving? If yes, what is the retention period and how is it configurable per-account?  
2) KV / cache traces: Are cache entries (KV caches used for session acceleration) written to durable storage or are they entirely in-memory/ephemeral?  
3) Training: Do you ever use customer-provided prompts or outputs to train models? If so, what opt-out mechanisms do you offer and how do you enforce them?  
4) Evidence: please point us to the SOC 2 AOC and any short diagram or note that shows storage lifecycle for telemetry related to requests.  

We need short, concrete answers plus evidence files (PDF/diagram). If it's easier, an annotated one-pager we can share with legal is fine. Appreciate a response within two business days if possible — the procurement review is on a tight schedule.

Best,
Oliver
Director, Information Security
Medica Health

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@medicahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: questions on logs, retention, training

Oliver — thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers and I attached a short evidence packet. I also looped in Marissa (customer success / commercial) and Rishi (security lead) for any contractual or technical clarifications.

1) Prompt/interaction logs: We do not use customer prompts or chat transcripts for model training by default. By policy, prompt-level request logs are retained for diagnostics and abuse detection for a default of 30 days; customers on enterprise plans can configure shorter retention (24h minimum) or elect a 'no-logs-for-training' mode which additionally prevents retention beyond request processing. Retention is policy-controlled per account and enforced by our access and lifecycle service.

2) KV / cache traces: KV caches used by the serving runtime are memory-resident and sharded across GPU workers. We do not write active KV cache contents to durable customer-accessible storage. For failover, a transient in-memory snapshot may be persisted to encrypted ephemeral disks for <12 hours during graceful node handoff; those snapshots are rotated and securely wiped post-failover. The diagram in the attachment shows the lifecycle.

3) Training on customer data: Redwood does not incorporate customer prompts, responses, or derived transcripts into model training or development datasets unless there is an explicit, opt-in agreement for model fine-tuning. For clarity: (a) default hosted API usage: no training usage; (b) if a customer signs a training opt-in addendum, we will only use de-identified aggregates and only with documented consent and DPA controls. Customers can request a guarantee in their DPA that no customer data will be used for training — we have a standard clause we will add to enterprise contracts.

4) Evidence: attached: redwood_sig_answers_v1.pdf (SIG answers), soc2_aoc_2027.pdf (SOC 2 AOC summary), ephemeral-storage-diagram.png (storage lifecycle).

If helpful I can provide a short one-paragraph attestation for legal or a stamped DPA clause to go into DocuSign. Let me know if you want that and Marissa will advise on the commercial placement.

— Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0132

Connor — thanks, that helps a lot. Two quick clarifications:  

• For the 30-day default: can you confirm whether backups (e.g., for disaster recovery) might extend that retention further?
• For the in-memory snapshots during failover: does your secure wipe satisfy NIST SP 800-88 guidelines, or can you share the wiping process?

If you can add two short bullets to the PDF that address those, great. Otherwise a short reply will do.

Oliver

Internal note / FYI — Connor: good answers. Procurement will likely ask for a firm DPA commitment around "no training" and a retention toggle. We can offer the following commercial levers: a standard DPA clause that guarantees no training unless explicitly opted-in, and an enterprise option for 24hr rolling retention with a small premium discount if they commit to a 12‑month reserved plan. Rishi: please confirm whether the wiping process language below is acceptable to ship in the customer-facing attestation.

Suggested wiping language (for attestation):

Action items: Connor — provide the two-line backup answer and confirm we can sign the DPA with the "no training" clause. Marissa — I'll draft the DPA language and pricing note.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: questions on logs, retention, training

Oliver / team — final confirmations below so you have a single-line summary to bring to procurement/legal.

• Backups: Our snapshot/backups are limited to configuration/state backups for cluster recovery and are retained separately from request logs. Backup retention windows are configurable; request logs are not included in long-term disaster-recovery backups by default. We will add a deployment note to the evidence packet that customer interaction logs are excluded from our durable DR backups unless a customer explicitly enables long-term logging.

• Wiping process: Confirmed — ephemeral volumes used during failover are encrypted and securely wiped following a process aligned to NIST SP 800-88 (clear + cryptographic erase as applicable). Rishi: happy to include a short procedural note you sign off on for the attestation.

Next steps: 1) Marissa to send the DPA with the "no training without opt-in" clause and the 24hr retention option; 2) Oliver / Medica to confirm they want the DPA and whether they prefer a redline or our standard clause; 3) I will upload a stamped attestation PDF to the Drive link and share DocuSign once we agree wording.
